sections.overview: This catalogue retains the name Pseudotropheus socolofi, now generally accepted as Chindongo socolofi. The cichlid is recorded along the Mozambican shore of Lake Malawi.
sections.identification: The name Pindani is used for this species.
sections.habitat: It inhabits shallow water over sand, with territorial males remaining near rocks.
sections.diet: It feeds on the biocover growing on rock and sand.
sections.behavior: Territorial males stay close to rocks.
sections.reproduction: Females incubate eggs in their mouths.
sections.ecology: Its distribution in Lake Malawi is limited to Mozambique in the FishBase record.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern from 2018.
